title: Electrochemical Cell Voltage Comparison Lab
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D electrochemistry lab using Three.js that compares voltages of electrochemical cells with different electrode materials and includes time-based simulation control.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a dark lab background (color #1a1a2e). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights for clear visibility.
- Load the 'robot.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Scale it to (0.8, 0.8, 0.8) and position it at (-6, 0, 0). This robot serves as the lab assistant. Give it a subtle idle bobbing animation (sinusoidal Y oscillation, amplitude 0.15, period 2s).
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.

ELECTROCHEMICAL CELLS:
- Create THREE electrochemical cells arranged in a row at X positions [-2, 1.5, 5]. Each cell consists of:
  - A transparent beaker (cylinder geometry, radius 0.8, height 1.5, transparent blue material, opacity 0.25) sitting on the ground plane (Y=0).
  - Two electrode plates inside each beaker (box geometry 0.08 x 1.0 x 0.5), one on the left (anode) and one on the right (cathode), separated by 0.6 units.
  - A wire connecting the tops of the electrodes (thin cylinder or line).
  - Electrolyte solution shown as a semi-transparent volume inside the beaker.

ELECTRODE MATERIALS (define standard reduction potentials):
- Cell 0: Zn/Cu cell — Zn anode (E°=-0.76V, gray), Cu cathode (E°=+0.34V, orange-brown). E°cell = 1.10V
- Cell 1: Fe/Ag cell — Fe anode (E°=-0.44V, dark gray), Ag cathode (E°=+0.80V, silver). E°cell = 1.24V
- Cell 2: Mg/Au cell — Mg anode (E°=-2.37V, light gray), Au cathode (E°=+1.50V, gold). E°cell = 3.87V

VOLTAGE SIMULATION WITH TIME CONTROL:
- Each cell has a simulated voltage that starts at 0V when the experiment begins.
- When the simulation is running, voltage ramps up over 3 seconds to the theoretical E°cell value, following a 1-exp(-t/tau) curve with tau=0.8s.
- After reaching steady state, voltage slowly decays at 0.5% per second to simulate electrode degradation.
- A global simulation clock tracks elapsed time in seconds (starting at 0).

TIME CONTROLS (DOM buttons):
- 'Start' button (id='btn-start'): begins the simulation. Sets running=true.
- 'Pause' button (id='btn-pause'): pauses simulation, freezing all voltages at current values.
- 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset'): resets simulation to t=0, all voltages to 0, running=false.
- 'Speed x1' / 'Speed x2' / 'Speed x5' buttons (ids: 'btn-speed-1', 'btn-speed-2', 'btn-speed-5'): change simulation speed multiplier.

CELL SELECTION & DISPLAY:
- Clicking on a beaker selects that cell (highlight with emissive glow). The selected cell index is stored.
- A HUD panel (id='hud-panel') on the right side shows: selected cell name, anode material, cathode material, current voltage (2 decimal places), theoretical voltage, elapsed time.
- A voltage bar chart (3 colored bars in a DOM div, id='voltage-chart') shows all three cell voltages as percentage of their theoretical max. Bar heights update in real-time.

KEYBOARD INTERACTIONS:
- Keys '1', '2', '3' select cell 0, 1, 2 respectively.
- Key 'S' toggles start/pause.
- Key 'R' resets the simulation.

VISUAL FEEDBACK:
- Electrode glow intensity proportional to current voltage / theoretical voltage.
- Bubble particles rise inside each beaker when simulation is running, with bubble rate proportional to voltage.
- Wire between electrodes glows brighter as voltage increases.

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- robotLoaded: boolean, true when robot.glb is loaded
- robotY: number, current robot Y position
- simRunning: boolean
- simTime: number (elapsed seconds, accounting for speed)
- speedMultiplier: number (1, 2, or 5)
- selectedCell: number (0, 1, or 2, default 0)
- cellVoltages: [number, number, number] — current voltage of each cell
- theoreticalVoltages: [1.10, 1.24, 3.87]
- cellNames: ['Zn/Cu', 'Fe/Ag', 'Mg/Au']
- cellCount: 3
- bubbleActive: boolean (true when sim running and voltages > 0)
- electrodeGlow: [number, number, number] — glow intensity 0-1 for each cell
- voltageBarHeights: [number, number, number] — percentage 0-100 for chart bars
- paused: boolean
- resetCount: number — how many times reset was pressed
physics_constraints: Voltage follows V(t) = E°cell * (1 - exp(-t/0.8)) during ramp-up phase (first ~3s). After reaching >99% of theoretical, voltage decays at 0.5% per second. All voltages must remain >= 0 and <= theoretical maximum. Electrode glow must be proportional to voltage ratio. Bubble rate must correlate with voltage magnitude. Time must advance proportionally to speedMultiplier.
